## Time constant

For a resistor and capacitor in series, the time constant sets the pace of charging and discharging:

$$
\tau = RC
$$

After one time constant, a charging capacitor reaches about 63.2% of its final value; after five, it's considered fully settled (99.3%).

## Charging from zero

Starting from 0 V toward a supply $V_s$:

$$
V(t) = V_s \left(1 - e^{-t/\tau}\right)
$$

Discharging back toward 0 V from $V_s$ follows the mirror image, $V(t) = V_s e^{-t/\tau}$.

## Calculator

Charging case, starting from 0 V.

```{=html}
<div id="rc-calc"></div>
<script src="../assets/js/calc-engine.js"></script>
<script>
Calc.create({
  root: "rc-calc",
  inputs: [
    { id: "R", label: "R (kΩ)", value: 10, min: 0.001, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "C", label: "C (µF)", value: 100, min: 0.001, step: 1 },
    { id: "Vs", label: "Vs (V)", value: 5, min: 0, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "t", label: "t (ms)", value: 1, min: 0, step: 0.1 }
  ],
  outputs: [
    { id: "tau", label: "Time constant τ" },
    { id: "vt", label: "V(t)" }
  ],
  compute: function (v) {
    var R = v.R * 1000;
    var C = v.C * 1e-6;
    var t = v.t / 1000;
    var tau = R * C;
    var vt = tau > 0 ? v.Vs * (1 - Math.exp(-t / tau)) : 0;
    var tauTxt = tau >= 1 ? tau.toFixed(3) + " s" : (tau * 1000).toFixed(2) + " ms";
    return {
      tau: tauTxt,
      vt: vt.toFixed(3) + " V"
    };
  }
});
</script>
```
